entities.summary:
Glaucus of Chios was a Greek metal sculptor from the island of Chios, who is often distinguished as the inventor of the art of soldering metals.

Born in the early 8th century BCE, Glaucus spent his formative years on the island of Chios, where he was exposed to the island's rich resources of tin and other metals.

He is credited with developing the technique of soldering, which allowed for the creation of more complex metalwork and paved the way for the development of more advanced technologies.

Glaucus's work had a significant impact on the development of metalwork in ancient Greece and beyond. His techniques were later adopted by other metalworkers, including the famous Greek sculptor, Phidias.

Glaucus's legacy extends beyond the world of metalwork, as his innovative techniques also influenced the development of other fields, such as architecture and engineering.

Glaucus of Chios was a key figure in the development of ancient Greek metalwork, and his contributions had a lasting impact on the art and technology of the time.

The exact dates of Glaucus's birth and death are unknown, but it is believed that he lived in the early 8th century BCE and died in 700 BCE.
